title: Pilot study to investigate the acceptance, feasibility, and efficacy of a hypnotherapeutic intervention for mothers of premature infants in daily farewell situations in the neonatal intensive care unit
summary:
Background:
In Germany, around 10,000 babies are born very prematurely each year—that is, before the 32nd week of pregnancy. These babies require treatment in a specialized neonatal intensive care unit (NICU). For mothers, this is a very distressing situation. They see their baby in a vulnerable condition and often experience fear, worry, helplessness, and uncertainty. One of the most difficult moments is leaving their baby behind after a visit to the intensive care unit and having to say goodbye.
Aim of the study:
This pilot study aims to examine whether two specific psychological support interventions based on methods of hypnotherapy can help mothers cope with these daily farewell situations. The study investigates whether these support interventions are more helpful than a comparison intervention or standard care alone, how well the interventions are accepted by mothers, and whether they can be feasibly implemented in everyday clinical practice.
Methods:
A total of 72 mothers will participate in the study. Their babies were born before the 32nd week of pregnancy and are expected to remain in the intensive care unit for more than two weeks. The study is conducted at three sites (Jena, Dresden, and Regensburg). The mothers are randomly assigned to one of four groups. In all groups, mothers record an audio message in their own voice. This recording is played over a loudspeaker before the mother leaves the unit on subsequent days, so that both mother and baby can hear it.
In Group 1 (18 mothers), mothers record a child-friendly farewell story, in Group 2 (18 mothers), mothers record a “sleep well ritual.” Both interventions include calming self-suggestions (a form of positive self-influence) intended to reduce fear and worry, decrease feelings of helplessness, and strengthen feelings of safety and personal competence.
In an active control group (18 mothers), mothers also record a story, but without any specific hypnotherapeutic elements. In addition, there is a group of mothers (18 mothers) who receive standard care only. This allows researchers to assess whether the new interventions provide additional benefits.
The study examines how effective the interventions are, how well they are accepted by mothers, how feasible they are in everyday clinical practice, and whether they are associated with any unwanted effects.
conditions: Mothers with preterm infants who need to be treated at the neonatal intensive care unit

interventions.name: Audio recording of a hypnotherapeutic farewell story by the study participants and playback of the audio recording before daily leaving the neonatal intensive care unit
Audio recording of a hypnotherapeutic ‘sleep well ritual’ by the study participants and playback of the audio recording before daily leaving the neonatal intensive care unit
Audio recording of a neutral story by the study participants and playback of the audio recording before daily leaving the neonatal intensive care unit
Standard treatment alone without audio recording

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Mothers of a premature baby (up to 32 weeks of pregnancy) who requires care in the neonatal intensive care unit
- Planned duration of neonatal intensive care: 14 days or more
- Mothers must be able to visit their child regularly (at least every other day)
Exclusion criteria:
- Insufficient knowledge of the German language
- Child in palliative care or with shunt care
- Participation in another clinical trial
